records.cycle_description: Individual CPA license renewal is a rolling 2-year 'reestablishment period' anchored to each CPA's own original certificate date, not a publicly stated odd/even calendar split. Fla. Admin. Code R. 61H1-33.003(1)(a) fixes the exact mechanism: the initial period runs to the third June 30 following the certificate date, and every period after that is a standard July 1 - June 30 two-year CPE cycle. The license itself renews December 31 of that same year (DBPR's renewal cycle runs October 1 - December 31 of the year the license expires) -- June 30 is the CPE reestablishment cutoff, not the renewal deadline. Real active licenses show both odd- and even-year expirations simultaneously (confirmed via DBPR's live license-verification tool) because of this personal anchor -- there is no single statewide date, but the exact date IS computable from your own certificate date.

computation.note: The initial CPE reestablishment period ends on the third June 30 strictly after your certificate date; every period after that rolls forward 2 years at a time. That June 30 is the CPE cutoff for the cycle -- the license itself renews December 31 of the same year (month/day above locate the CPE-anchored cycle year; renewal_month/renewal_day is the date actually due).

records.cycle_description: CPA permits expire December 31 of the year the Board assigns to each licensee and renew triennially (ORC 4701.10(A): 'All Ohio permits shall expire on the last day of December of the year assigned by the board'). Because assigned years are spread across the three-year cycle, only about a third of Ohio CPAs are due in any given year. The Board's renewal window runs from early October to December 31; a late filing fee accrues for each month after expiration, so do not count on a grace period.
records.grace_period_note: No grace period is codified. ORC 4701.10(D)-(E) impose a late filing fee for each full month or part of a month after the expiration date, and the Board's renewal window closes December 31 -- so treat December 31 as the real deadline.

records.cycle_description: Biennial (every 2 years), expiring June 30. The Commonwealth's official Division of Occupational Licensure fee/renewal-schedule page for the Public Accountancy board (licensing.reg.state.ma.us) confirms 'Biennial (2 years)' and '30-Jun / ODD & EVEN YEAR' for individual CPAs, i.e. renewals are split across odd and even years board-wide. CPE is 80 hours per 2-year period (4 hours ethics, no carryover) per 252 CMR 2.14. Once a license is on a given parity (odd or even year), the Board's own reinstatement guidance confirms it stays on that parity permanently -- every renewal is exactly 2 years later on the same parity, never a genuinely opaque board-assigned split. Which parity a NEW license starts on is strongly suggested (not yet independently confirmed by an explicit rule statement) by the Board's own first-renewal CPE-proration table -- see the sourcing note below for the exact reasoning and why we are not yet computing a specific date from it.

computation.note: Strong hypothesis, not yet confirmed to ship as computed: first renewal = the SECOND June 30 strictly after the license's issuance date (same shape as Florida's confirmed 'third June 30' rule, but N=2); every renewal after that is a standard 2-year rollover on the same parity thereafter. records.data_gap_note: UPGRADED 2026-08-19 (was previously treated as genuinely unresolvable -- that framing was too pessimistic, see below): this is NOT a board-assigned-opaque split like Michigan/Ohio. The Board's own FAQ publishes a first-renewal CPE-proration table (80/70/60/50 hours depending on issuance quarter: Jul-Sep/Oct-Dec/Jan-Mar/Apr-Jun) that reconciles almost exactly (each quarter's implied month-count rounds to the nearest 10 CPE hours at the stated 80hrs/24mo rate) with a 'first renewal = the second June 30 strictly after issuance' rule -- the same shape as Florida's confirmed 'third June 30' mechanism, just N=2 instead of N=3. This is a strong numerical fit across all 4 independent data points from an official Board table, but it is an INFERENCE from a CPE-hours proration table, not a statute/regulation explicitly stating the expiration-date rule itself (unlike Florida, where the 'third June 30' language is directly in the codified rule text) -- so we are not shipping a computed date on this basis alone. records.cycle_description: Firm permits are issued/renewed for terms of up to two years, always expiring June 30, but which calendar year applies to a given firm depends on when that firm's permit was last issued or renewed AND which term length (1 or 2 years) it was issued for -- both printed on the firm's own permit, not published per-firm by the board (NMSA 1978, 61-28B-13(E), as amended by Laws 2025, ch. 105 (HB 296)).

computation.note: Next deadline = June 30, (year your permit was last issued/renewed) + (the 1- or 2-year term printed on that same permit). Unlike Washington/Puerto Rico, the term itself varies per permit -- not a fixed state-wide constant -- so this is a single-shot calculation from the firm's own two permit facts, not a repeating rollover.
